I changed `runDaemonForContext` in `packages/playwright/src/mcp/test/browserBackend.ts` so it exposes each browser to the CLI only once. I haven't built or run anything, so the fix is untested.

The function used to call `browser.bind(...)` every time a context was created. The second call threw the "browser server already running" error. It now keeps a `WeakSet` of browsers it has already bound. A context created on an already-bound browser returns `false` right away. It skips the bind, the session-name print and the pause request.

Only the first context on a browser prints the session name and pauses. Later contexts, such as the one from your worker-scoped fixture, just run.

I didn't check whether `bind()` still works after the context that triggered it has closed. That could matter if the first context closes before a later one is created.
